 Follow Is Halloween a federal holiday? What’s open and closed today
 Catherine Messier, USA TODAY NETWORK - New England Sat, October 31, 2026 at 9:09 AM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Halloween is here, falling on Saturday, Oct. 31. But despite being one of the country's most recognizable celebrations, Halloween isn't a federal holiday.
 That means Halloween itself doesn't trigger the widespread closures associated with holidays such as Thanksgiving, Christmas or New Year's Day. However, since Halloween falls on a Saturday this year, many people will have the day off and some entitites that are only open on weekdays will be closed in accordance with their normal schedule.
 So are banks, post offices and businesses open on Halloween? And does anyone officially get the day off? Here's what to know.
 Is Halloween a federal holiday?
 Will Nunnery of Kennedy Country Gardens on Rt. 3A in Scituate works on an early Halloween display at the greenhouse on Wednesday, September 23, 2026 No, Halloween is not a federal holiday. Although Halloween is widely celebrated across the country, it is not recognized as an official holiday on the federal or state level.
 Are businesses closed on Halloween?
 Businesses are typically open on Halloween.
 Is the stock market open on Halloween?
 Because Halloween 2026 falls on a Saturday, the stock market will be closed, as it always is on Saturdays.
 Will mail be delivered on Halloween?
 As mail is typically delivered on Saturdays, you can expect your mail to arrive at usual on Halloween.

 What is a federal holiday?
 Federal holidays are holidays that are officially recognized by the United States government. All federal holidays are paid days off for federal employees, with closures observed at federal offices, financial institutions, schools and certain businesses.

 When are the federal holidays of 2026?
 The United States currently recognizes 11 holidays as federal holidays . Here are the holidays and their dates in 2026:
 New Year's Day – Thursday, Jan. 1
 Martin Luther King, Jr. Day – Monday, Jan. 19
 Washington's Birthday/Presidents Day – Monday, Feb. 16
 Memorial Day – Monday, May 25
 Juneteenth – Friday, June 19
 Independence Day – Saturday, July 4
 Labor Day – Monday, Sept. 7
 Columbus Day/Indigenous People's Day – Monday, Oct. 12
 Veterans Day – Wednesday, Nov. 11
 Thanksgiving Day – Thursday, Nov. 26
 Christmas Day – Friday, Dec. 25
